source.title: EASE: Practical and Efficient Safety Alignment for Small Language Models
source.authors: Haonan Shi; Guoli Wang; Tu Ouyang; An Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small chat models with safety reasoning and evaluates harmful-response attack success rates under several jailbreak methods. This is a different intervention and evaluation from the claim’s original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack success rates for EASE and the original instruct models on AdvBench under HumanJailbreak, PAP, PAIR, and no attack. It does not test harmful-response fine-tuning, benign-only fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant-prefill bypasses, decoding changes, or parameter localization.
record.test_reason: The paper borrows the label 'shallow alignment' (citing Qi et al.) to mean refusal training without reasoning. It then reports its own method (EASE, safety-reasoning distillation with calibration) against instruct, refusal-training and deliberative-alignment baselines. It never measures token-position depth (V3/V7), harmful or benign fine-tuning attacks (V1/V2), or opening bypasses such as prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes (V4). Its attacks (HumanJailbreak, PAP, PAIR) are prompt-level semantic jailbreaks, not attacks that get past the response opening. The EASE-versus-instruct rows compare the authors' own method with baselines, not a test of whether deepening safety beyond the first tokens works.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that EASE, with selective safety reasoning, gives small models robust protection against sophisticated jailbreaks and preserves general-task capability. The abstract quantifies this as jailbreak ASR up to 17% lower than shallow (refusal) alignment and inference overhead up to 90% lower than deliberative alignment.
record.recipe_differences: EASE distills policy-guided safety reasoning and then calibrates when reasoning is activated; it is not a test of the original papers’ fine-tuning, token-position KL, or compliant-prefill recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack type and model affect ASR; the reported ASRs vary across HumanJB, PAP, and PAIR and across the three models.

fits_no_version.finding: Distilled safety reasoning cut prompt-jailbreak ASR on AdvBench (HumanJB/PAP/PAIR) from 12–44% on instruct SLMs to 0–6%. On WildJailbreak and DAN, reasoning-based alignment gave roughly half the ASR of refusal training (Tables 1–2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-based (deliberative) safety alignment makes small models more robust to semantic jailbreaks than refusal training.

record.problems: AdvBench attack evaluation uses a refined subset of 50 prompts, and the paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed ASRs. The attack evaluation does not cover compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports additional safety-benchmark ASRs, but its values are flattened in the supplied text and cannot be reliably assigned to each method and dataset. General-task accuracy, token counts, reasoning rates, and ablation results do not directly measure the tested versions and are omitted.

untested.parts: No benign-only fine-tuning with a measured effect on harmful compliance.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial-suffix or decoding-change attacks; only semantic prompt jailbreaks.
No analysis of what data or objective causes token-level shallowness.
Safety depth across response positions is never measured, and EASE is not evaluated against prefilling or fine-tuning attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 and V7 links rest on a terminology overlap. Here 'shallow alignment' means refusal without reasoning, not safety concentrated in the first response tokens. No attack in the paper manipulates the response opening, and no depth measurement is made. All rows are therefore relinked to none, and no verdicts are given. Table 1 ASRs are similarly off-version.

versions.untested_parts: The refusal-training baseline uses harmful prompts paired with safe answers; it does not fine-tune on harmful answers to test whether a few to a few hundred examples remove refusals.
Benign examples appear in mixed calibration training, but the paper does not isolate benign-only fine-tuning or measure its effect on harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis is reported.
The paper evaluates HumanJailbreak, PAP, and PAIR attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization experiment is reported.
The study does not test whether data or a training objective causes token-level shallowness.
The study trains safety reasoning and evaluates attack outcomes, but does not measure whether safety is distributed beyond the first response tokens or isolate token-depth as the cause.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Original instruct models under HumanJailbreak, PAP, and PAIR on AdvBench
reader_labels.reason: These attacks produced nonzero ASRs of 12.0%–44.0% on the original instruct models (T2-Q15-BASE-HJB, T2-Q15-BASE-PAP, T2-Q15-BASE-PAIR, T2-Q3-BASE-HJB, T2-Q3-BASE-PAP, T2-Q3-BASE-PAIR, T2-L3-BASE-HJB, T2-L3-BASE-PAP, T2-L3-BASE-PAIR).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: EASE models under the same attacks
reader_labels.reason: EASE reduced ASR substantially; several attack/model combinations had zero ASR, while others retained only 2.0%–6.0% (T2-Q15-EASE-HJB, T2-Q15-EASE-PAP, T2-Q15-EASE-PAIR, T2-Q3-EASE-HJB, T2-Q3-EASE-PAP, T2-Q3-EASE-PAIR, T2-L3-EASE-HJB, T2-L3-EASE-PAP, T2-L3-EASE-PAIR). The tested attacks were not compliant-prefill or decoding-change tests.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: EASE models on the tested AdvBench attack conditions
reader_labels.reason: After EASE safety-reasoning training, ASR was lower than on the corresponding instruct models under every listed attack; values were 0.0%–6.0% (T2-Q15-EASE-NONE, T2-Q15-EASE-HJB, T2-Q15-EASE-PAP, T2-Q15-EASE-PAIR, T2-Q3-EASE-NONE, T2-Q3-EASE-HJB, T2-Q3-EASE-PAP, T2-Q3-EASE-PAIR, T2-L3-EASE-NONE, T2-L3-EASE-HJB, T2-L3-EASE-PAP, T2-L3-EASE-PAIR).
